description.value: Boat- or kayak-in group campsite at the north end of Sidney Island in Gulf Islands National Park Reserve, with sandy beaches, wooded trails, and abundant birdlife and marine life; inaccessible to loaded touring cyclists without a boat.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The Parks Canada website confirms Sidney Spit Campground exists on Sidney Island within Gulf Islands National Park Reserve and is accessible only by boat or kayak — not by bicycle without a water-crossing. The OSM record specifically names the Group Campsite variant, and the website confirms reservations are accepted (2026 reservation launch announced). No amenity details specific to this group campsite are provided on the webpage; the SMONEĆTEN (McDonald) Campground is the one explicitly called out as suitable for cyclists, not Sidney Spit.
concerns: Campsite is on Sidney Island and explicitly accessible only by boat or kayak — no bicycle-direct land access.
OSM record names the Group Campsite specifically; the website describes the site in aggregate without group-specific amenity details.
No phone or address in OSM record; Parks Canada general inquiry number (1-888-773-8888) exists on website but is not site-specific.

Cabbage Island camping (a nearby Parks Canada site) noted as closed until further notice — confirms some Gulf Islands sites have reduced services; Sidney Spit status not separately flagged but worth monitoring.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Sidney Spit is accessible only by boat or kayak, making it a non-standard cycling destination; it could suit Gulf Islands cycle-tourers combining cycling with water-taxi crossings, but the group-only format and marine-only access warrant human review before inclusion in a cycling tourism directory.
enrichment_extras.notes: The SMONEĆTEN (McDonald) Campground on Vancouver Island is the Parks Canada Gulf Islands site explicitly described as suitable for cyclists and RVers — that record may be a stronger WWC candidate than this one.

wow_evidence: Gulf Islands National Park Reserve … accessible only by boat or kayak
